findings.F1: In agitated bars (folds B, C), the 7-day excess return over the coin's mean is concentrated in the top fifth of closes by place in the day's range: +5.82 % (t 2.53, same-day cases together, 130 cases on 55 days). The next three fifths give -2.61 %, -0.93 % and +0.19 % (t -1.13, -0.45, 0.08). The effect is therefore not graded across the upper half of the range, which is where the tested forecast was positive. On the same B, C cases, that forecast earned only +1.11 % (t 0.68, 370 cases), and +0.28 % (t 0.30) on all folds.
findings.F2: The top-fifth effect is not the first day. From day 2 to day 7 the top fifth still gains +5.83 % excess (t 2.45, 55 days). Meanwhile, the next day the top fifth falls -0.64 % (t -2.97, 898 cases) and the bottom fifth rises +0.84 % (t 3.89). This is the brief's sequence: a one-day payback, then a week following the side that won.
findings.F3: The top-minus-bottom gap over 7 days is consistent across subsets. The top fifth is positive in every year shown: 2018 +5.6 %, 2019 +2.1 %, 2020 +5.7 %, 2021 +7.6 %. It is positive on 9 of 10 coins, from BTC +5.8 % to ADA +15.5 %, with TRX -2.4 % the exception. It is positive in every 20-day trend: down +3.8 %, flat +5.9 %, up +7.2 % (t 2.36).
findings.F4: The same top fifth in calm bars gives +2.82 % (t 1.21, 62 days), about half the agitated move and not distinguishable from 0. The agitated profile the brief names carries the effect.
findings.F5: The signal is one day's close, not a run of them. The 3-day mean of close location shows no ordering over 7 days: top fifth +0.59 % (t 0.24), bottom fifth +0.18 % (t 0.09).

findings.F7: The book moves with the coins. Its daily returns correlate 0.81 with the coins' mean. On its worst 2 % of days the coins fell -12.7 %, and on its best 2 % they rose +11.6 %, so its gain is mostly the market's.

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, a daily close at the very top of that day's high-to-low range is followed, from the next day, by a rise over the following 6 days. The rise grows steeply the smaller the gap between the close and the day's high, as a share of the day's range, and is largest when the close sits at the high itself.
ideas.consequence: Buy an agitated coin only when it closes right at its day's high, not merely in the upper half, and skip the first day's payback. The week's rise per case (about 6 % in folds B, C) covers a 0.22 % trade many times over.
ideas.name: agitated top close week rise
